notes.overview: The LMU wiki guide is written for the full Grand Prix layout; the National circuit shares its Copse, Maggotts, Becketts, Brooklands, Luffield and Woodcote corners, and only that advice is carried here. It is a fast, flowing, aero-dependent track that rewards smooth inputs and looking after the front tyres; in a Hypercar, stability under braking and a settled aero platform matter most. Typical mistakes are overdriving the fast Maggotts-Becketts run, over-trail-braking into Brooklands, getting on the throttle too early at Luffield, and leaning too hard on the kerbs. The guide suggests a medium to high rear wing and a forward brake bias for GT3, and a medium wing with slightly stiffer suspension and a slightly rearward bias for Hypercar.

corners.1: Copse, a high-speed right-hander. A light brake or just a lift, depending on fuel load; do not over-brake. Keep the car neutral and take an early apex without pinching the entry. A Hypercar is close to flat on low fuel but usually needs a small lift in race trim: keep the steering angle small, avoid a sharp brake stab, and set up the exit position.
corners.2: Maggotts, a fast left-hander. In a GT3 a slight lift before the apex, stay right over to the left and use as little steering as possible. In a Hypercar a short lift settles the front; keep the steering very smooth, because mid-corner corrections upset the aero balance.
corners.3: Becketts. Commit on entry and lift only if the car needs it for stability; rhythm and balance pay more than aggression here. A Hypercar arrives much faster than a GT3 and may need a light brake before the right-hander; do not over-rotate it or the aero platform goes unsettled.
corners.4: Brooklands, the stop at the end of the long straight. GT3: brake at the flag-light on the right and trail-brake to rotate the car, keeping a tidy line to set up Luffield. Hypercar: heavy braking with a strong initial pressure, then trail off carefully because the rear gets unstable; rotate early so you are not correcting mid-corner.
corners.5: Luffield, a long, slow right-hander. Brake in a straight line with just a little trail braking, rotate the car first, then add throttle progressively. Be patient: early throttle here is a classic mistake, and heavy kerb use unsettles the rear. In a Hypercar keep the steering angle small once the car has turned and avoid overheating the rear tyres on exit.
corners.6: Woodcote, taken flat out. Use the full width of the track and keep the steering smooth to protect aero efficiency.
